title: Introduce affinity-aware onboarding scorer and release-threader for stitched changelogs
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: onboarding throughput and reviewer bandwidth are limited during model intake bursts. We need a deterministic, explainable way to rank incoming model candidates so that profiling, human review, and compute-heavy sampling are allocated to models that maximize coverage and mitigate risk earlier. Additionally, onboarding currently emits multiple small changelog fragments (profiling notes, evaluation blips, policy checks) that are hard to consume. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an affinity-aware onboarding scorer that computes a 'priority_score' for each intake based on resource affinity, expected sample cost, usage signal, and sensitivity heuristics; and (2) a release-threader service that stitches micro-changelog pieces into a concise, human-friendly release thread for the model record and for team-facing release notes. Implementation summary: added a new scoring module (src/onboard/affinity_scorer.py) implementing a configurable weighted scoring pipeline; introduced a DB migration to persist priority_score and score_metadata (migrations/20250210_add_priority_score.sql); new API endpoints (/onboard/priority, /release-threader/compose) and a background worker that enqueues prioritization jobs and composes threads; small changes to the intake pipeline to emit canonical micro-changelog fragments (src/onboard/micro_changelog_writer.py); release-threader templating and heuristics live in services/release_threader/ and include rules to collapse low-signal fragments into an "appendix" section. Observability: metrics onboarding.priority_seconds, onboarding.queue_wait_by_priority, threader.compose_duration, and a new tracing span for compose_thread; logs include deterministic score reasons for auditability. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated (flags.onboard.affinity_scorer, flags.release.threader), staged canary at 10% of intake traffic for 48 hours, metric checks (queue latency, reviewer throughput, thread size) before full rollout. Backwards compatibility: micro-changelog fragments are additive and the migration is non-destructive; services fallback to previous behavior if feature flags are off. Checklist: - [x] Scorer algorithm implemented and unit tested - [x] DB migration script added and backwards-safe - [x] Release-threader service implemented and integration tested - [x] E2E test in staging validating composed thread format - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts seeded - [x] Feature flags and rollout doc added Related: ties to ENG-4821 intake backlog prioritization and ENG-4987 changelog consolidation.

release_notes:
- Add affinity-aware onboarding priority scoring to triage model intakes; produces explainable 'priority_score' and score_metadata for audit.
- Introduce release-threader service that composes micro-changelog fragments into a single release thread (compact and expanded modes).
- New DB migration to persist priority_score; non-destructive and feature-flag gated.
- Observability: onboarding.priority_seconds, threader.compose_duration, and new trace spans.
migration: migrations/20250210_add_priority_score.sql: adds nullable priority_score (float) and score_metadata (jsonb) to onboarding_requests; backfill job included as a separate cancellable migration (scripts/backfill_priority_from_signals.py).
testing: Unit tests for scorer and threader, integration test that runs the intake pipeline end-to-end in CI staging, and a small smoke harness that composes 100 micro-fragments to validate compact template size limits.
notes: Feature-flagged; rollout doc at docs/onboarding/affinity-scorer-rollout.md. This PR intentionally avoids changing existing released APIs; behaviour can be toggled off immediately if regressions are observed.
impact_assessment: Expected reduction in median reviewer queue time by ~28% in internal staging traffic (measured in experiments). Cost impact: small increase in compute for scoring (<0.05% of intake CPU) but reduced wasted profiling on low-value intakes. No breaking changes.
